prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up and handoff for aircraft loading. The boundary includes conveyance, screening, routing, reconciliation, staging and controls. It excludes airline loading beyond the outbound load control point. Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, delivery within cutoffs. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (oversees flow and recovery with the Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician). Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager (security). Airline Ramp Coordinator (accepts staged bags; sends the Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized). Staff verify eligibility, data, size and weight, held bags and transfer tags. Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records accepted bags; sends the Oversize Exception Ticket; oversize bags are held until a route is approved). Bag Tag Printer (unique durable tag). Transfer Bag Feeder (records transfer bags; sends the Late Transfer Bag Card). Induction Tray Conveyor (controlled spacing for separation and image capture). Interlocks stop feed on jam, open access door or loss of downstream readiness. Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (links the tag to passenger and flight; checks the flight is open; compares transfer routing; applies the screening profile from tag data and configuration; routes exception bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute avoiding outbound flows). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (grants the induction permissive; produces the Recovery Route Card). Flight Data Gateway (supplies flight and routing data; sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory). Screening: North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel (reads the bag ID at network entry). South Gate Scanner (independent read point on its path; produces the Manual Rescan Receipt). Both scanners acquire images, return a disposition per bag, and record image quality and alarm status. Image Resolution Desk: staff review unresolved images using full image, ID and prompts, then record a disposition. Secondary Inspection Chute: occupancy-monitored; no release into a blocked position. Sorting: Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (routes inducted bags per active routing data and current disposition; maintains identity; routes to make-up). Bag Reconciliation Station. Make-up and handoff: East and West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit; Outbound Load Control Desk (confirms readiness). Requirements: hold bags with bad data before induction; induct only with a valid record, available route and ready equipment. An incomplete exam is never treated as

Document units:
S066: Access to the Secondary Inspection Chute and its associated work area is limited to personnel with authorized duties.
S067: Explosives Response Team responds to escalated alarms and coordinates any required safety controls with airport security personnel.
S068: In local radio traffic, Explosives Response Team is also called Pebble.
S069: Inspection staff maintain physical control of an alarmed bag and do not return it to the sorter until an authorized disposition is recorded.
S070: The Bag Reconciliation Station verifies that the bag presented for examination matches the screening record before further handling.
S071: If an examination requires the bag to remain isolated, staff secure the area and notify the Baggage Operations Supervisor.
S072: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates decisions that affect flight readiness, staffing, or continued operation of a screening lane.
S073: The Security Duty Manager is notified when an alarm response requires a security decision beyond routine screening procedures.
S074: The Bag Tag Printer produces a Calibration Witness Tag when a calibration witness record is required.
S075: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is also known locally as Orchard.
S076: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit accepts only bags with a valid screening disposition and an authorized routing instruction.
S077: The Transfer Bag Feeder holds transfer bags from release until their screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S078: Staff return a bag to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization are consistent in the operating record.
S079: The Baggage Control System loads the approved sort plan and applies its effective time window before bags enter sortation.
S080: Lantern is the operational alias used for the Flight Data Gateway in sortation coordination.
S081: The Baggage Control System checks the plan against current flight and handling records before assigning a route.
S082: The Concourse Zone Controller coordinates local conveyor availability with the active sort plan.
S083: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags at controlled spacing so each bag can be identified before route selection.
S084: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter applies the assigned destination and screening status to each identified bag.
S085: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter sends a Chute Occupancy Note when a destination lane approaches its configured limit.
S086: Route selection favors the approved path with adequate capacity and sufficient time for the planned handling.
S087: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner verify bag identity at their respective route decision points.
